Definition: from the same as G221; Alexandrine, or belonging to Alexandria:--of Alexandria.
BiblicalUsage: A man from Alexandria, the great city of Egypt where the library stood and the Greek Old Testament was translated. In Acts the Alexandrians argue with Stephen in the synagogue of the Libertines, and cannot resist the wisdom and the spirit by which he speaks; and Apollos comes to Ephesus, an eloquent man from Alexandria, mighty in the Scriptures, and Priscilla and Aquila take him aside and explain the way of God more perfectly.
TheologicalSignificance: A name for a man from Alexandria carries no lesson of its own. What it shows is how far the gospel had already travelled, that Jews from Egypt were arguing in Jerusalem and a learned man from Alexandria was preaching Christ in Ephesus, and the Scriptures he knew were the same ones Stephen died for.
